A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same audit framework and retain identifiable original experiments despite the changed title and expanded scope. All pages, figures, tables, equations, and appendices were readable and supported comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-model audits, temperature experiments, URL/domain overlap analyses, and manual validation of 177 prompts in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds evaluations of seven additional models, benchmark construction results, and a guardrail experiment.

M1.justification: The four-stage audit, synthesis template, and URL-detector ensemble remain unchanged. However, v1 Section 3 describes prompt oracle P as an LLM classifier with author verification, while Section 4 already describes human review; v2 consistently specifies human annotation. The PDFs do not establish whether an LLM classification step was removed or its description corrected.

E1.justification: The MetaMask/PhishFort sources and developer code-generation domains are retained; Innoc2Scam-bench selects from the existing synthesized prompts. v2 additionally evaluates safe/unsafe classification of prompts and generated code through a guardrail, adding a defensive screening task in Appendix G.

E2.justification: v2 adds one evaluated defensive comparison: NeMo Guardrails using Llama Nemotron Safety Guard V2, tested on prompts and malicious outputs in Appendix G and Table 6. v1 contains no corresponding guardrail evaluation. The additional production LLMs are audit targets rather than competing audit frameworks.

E3.justification: v1's reported selection excludes matching seed/output domains and validates 191 candidates, retaining 177. v2 reports a different construction pipeline: three-annotator validation of 3,150 candidates followed by sampling according to explicit scam references to construct 1,559 prompts. It also adds seven target models with 20,000-token limits, completed/filtered/other outcome accounting, and a separate guardrail testing protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of explicit versus implicit scam references, filtering and incomplete-generation patterns, guardrail failure categories, and a worked YoMix case spanning the original and additional models (Appendices E, G, and H). The original temperature experiment, overlap analyses, and pump.fun mechanism discussion are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report prompt-hashed seeds and the same deterministic sampling convention. Neither reports repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's qualitative caveat about hosted-API nondeterminism does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The original malicious-program counts and rates match between v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 1, although v2 removes many corresponding URL/domain statistics. New results include benchmark rates of 12.7% for Gemini-2.5-Pro through 43.8% for DeepSeek-Chat-V3.1, negligible guardrail detection, and 62 accepted phishing-domain submissions. These benchmark results use selected prompts and are not directly comparable with the original approximately 4.24% audit rate.

T1.justification: The binary oracle definitions and set S of innocuous-prompt/malicious-code pairs remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive derivation or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: v2 makes Innoc2Scam-bench a third central contribution and extends the main claims to vulnerability persistence across seven additional production models and inadequate guardrail protection. The abstract and conclusion now emphasize these benchmark and defense findings alongside the retained automated-audit contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning model safety tiers, explicit scam references, and the roles of refusals and non-code responses in reported malicious-output rates (Section 6 and Appendix E). It also adds an API nondeterminism caveat. Conversely, v1's specific discussion of incomplete oracle coverage and disagreement between detectors is removed.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the previously undisclosed code-generation template, OpenRouter access information, model identifiers, token limits, and the complete guardrail policy prompt (Appendices A, B, and G). Section 9 expands access information to framework code, experimental data, accepted domain submissions, and the benchmark. The original audit's 2,000-token limit is newly documented, not an established change to that experiment.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Uncurated Datasets subsection and several scaling/data-exhaustion references, while adding NeMo Guardrails and supporting model/API references. The central positioning against inference-time contamination and prior training-data poisoning research remains, with clearer emphasis on auditing existing production models.

P1.justification: The paper is renamed around Scam2Prompt and substantially reorganized around dataset construction and benchmark evaluation. The abstract, contributions, and conclusion are rewritten; experimental details and analyses move into expanded appendices; and a reproducibility section replaces the earlier discussion-centered organization.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two-column to single-column layout, redraws the conversation example as a figure, restructures the main results table, and adds a dataset-construction diagram, benchmark and guardrail tables, prompt boxes, and extensive code listings. The original framework diagram and overlap plots are retained with relocation and resizing.

improvement.justification: The guardrail experiment supplies direct evidence for a defense limitation that v1 largely asserted, while additional model evaluations and implementation disclosures improve empirical support and reproducibility. These gains are limited by unresolved accounting discrepancies: Section 5 reports 1,165 non-explicit prompts while the evaluation uses 1,159, and Tables 5 and 6 contain unexplained differences in malicious-code totals. Removal of the oracle-coverage limitation also weakens qualification of the findings.
